categories.name: Whose Lantern Is Lit
categories.tagline: Presence and the friend list: knowing who is about, and saying what you are up to, without the game telling anyone.

ideas.title: Status Presets
ideas.pitch: Save a handful of status-and-note pairs and switch between them with one click or one short command.
ideas.experience: Raid night: you type /lantern as raid and your lantern goes busy with 'prog, back at 23:00'. Afterwards /lantern as chill flips it to online with 'maps? roulettes?'. Your static sees the note change in their list within one heartbeat.
ideas.audience: raiders, statics, anyone who forgets to change their note
ideas.how: Add a List<StatusPreset> (name, presence, note) to Configuration. Command.Parse gains an 'as <preset>' verb beside ParseStatus; Plugin.OnCommand resolves it and calls the existing LanternService.SetPresence. MainWindow.DrawMe gets a small preset combo next to the presence combo and note field. Parsing is BCL-only, so it is host-tested in XivLantern.Core.Tests like the rest of Commands.
ideas.risks: Very little. Preset names must not collide with existing subcommands (on, off, invite), so they sit behind 'as'. Notes are still typed text and are clamped by the same length limit.

ideas.title: Away When You Walk Off
ideas.pitch: Opt in, and your lantern dims to away after a few minutes with no keyboard or mouse input, and lights again when you come back.
ideas.experience: You leave the game running and go to make tea. Ten minutes later your friends see you as away with the note you left. You touch the mouse and you are online again before anyone asks.
ideas.audience: everyone who leaves the client open
ideas.how: A Framework.Update tick in LanternService (it already polls lt_poll there) checks OS idle time through GetLastInputInfo, never game state, and calls SetPresence with LT_PRESENCE_AWAY once past a threshold set in Configuration, restoring the previous presence and note on input. Off by default, shown in DrawSettings with the other switches.
ideas.risks: GetLastInputInfo under Wine reports X11/Wayland input only as well as Wine forwards it; controller-only players may look idle while playing. It must never override a status the player set by hand (busy, invisible), and the banned-API test in CoreTests must keep passing, so no IClientState shortcuts.

ideas.title: Up For It Tags
ideas.pitch: Tick a few typed tags (maps, roulettes, crafting, ex, chat) and friends can filter the list to people who want the same thing tonight.
ideas.experience: You fancy a treasure map run. You tick 'maps', open the list and filter by it: two friends lit up with the same tag. One message later you have a party, and nobody had to shout in an FC channel.
ideas.audience: friend groups, FCs, casual players
ideas.how: Extend Wire::Heartbeat in crates/lantern-core/src/node/friends.rs with a tags field, or better add a new Heartbeat2 variant at the end of the enum so old nodes keep decoding, and store tags beside status/note for each friend device. Surface them in lt_friend_list JSON, FriendView and GetFriends over IPC. MainWindow.DrawList gains a filter chip row. Tags are chosen from a fixed list plus free text the player types; nothing comes from the game.
ideas.risks: A wire change needs a compatibility plan: postcard enums break if variants are reordered, and mixed versions will run side by side for weeks. Free-text tags need the same clamping and ChatText.Clean treatment as notes. Tempting to auto-fill from the duty finder, which the design forbids.

ideas.title: Friend Folders
ideas.pitch: Sort friends into your own folders (static, FC, crafting pals) that collapse and show how many in each are lit.
ideas.experience: Your list has grown to thirty. Now it reads 'Static 6/8', 'FC 3/14', 'Old server 0/5'. You collapse the old server folder and the people who matter tonight are at the top.
ideas.audience: people with long friend lists, FC officers
ideas.how: Groups are local only: a Dictionary<string, string> from node id to folder in Configuration, never sent to anyone. MainWindow.DrawList renders ImGui.CollapsingHeader per folder with an online count from service.Friends, and a right-click menu on a friend to move them. Mutes keep using the existing Muted keys, so a folder can be muted in one step by toggling each key.
ideas.risks: Folders keyed by node id split when a friend reinstalls (new NodeId), until nostr device lists merge devices into one person. Drag and drop in Dalamud ImGui is fiddly; a context menu is the safer first cut.

ideas.title: Glance at the Server Bar
ideas.pitch: Hover the Lantern entry in the server info bar to see who is lit and their notes, without opening the window.
ideas.experience: Mid-dungeon, the bar says 'Lantern 3 · 1 unread'. You hover it: 'Alice, away: crafting', 'Bob, online', 'Cid, busy: prog'. You finish the pull and answer later.
ideas.audience: everyone, especially people who keep the window closed
ideas.how: Notifier already owns the IDtrBarEntry and refreshes its text on a timer from service.Friends and Book.TotalUnread. Set the entry's Tooltip to a short roster built by a pure function in XivLantern.Core (sorted online first, names through ChatText.Label, notes through ChatText.Preview) so it is host-tested. Clicking still calls toggleWindow.
ideas.risks: Tooltips are SeString, so friend-typed names and notes must be escaped so they cannot inject payloads or colour codes. Long lists need a cap ('and 7 more'). Hidden while streaming would be a sensible option, since the bar is often on screen.

categories.name: Linkshells of Your Own
categories.tagline: Channels you make and hand out, grown into something a static or FC can live in.

ideas.title: Catch Up on Join
ideas.pitch: Someone who joins or comes back to a channel gets the recent backlog from any member who has it, instead of an empty room.
ideas.experience: You log in after work and open #static. Instead of silence you see the last hour: the pull times, the strat link, 'who has the sprint macro?'. Each line still carries its author's verified signature.
ideas.audience: statics, FCs, anyone in a channel across time zones
ideas.how: DESIGN.md already names the shape: a blob snapshot offered by any member. Keep the signed gossip frames per channel in a new store table, and on a peer's Hello offer a snapshot with lt_blob_add_bytes and lt_blob_offer, which exist in the C ABI and the C# binding (BlobAddBytes, BlobOffer, BlobFetch) but are unused by the plugin today. The joiner fetches, re-verifies every frame with proto.rs, de-duplicates by signature and merges into ChatBook through Conversation.LoadHistory.
ideas.risks: Gossip gives no ordering, so merged history needs a sort by sender timestamp that a member could lie about. Every member keeps a copy, which makes 'delete' meaningless and should be said plainly. Snapshot size and how far back need limits, and a malicious member can offer junk, so verification must drop anything unsigned.

ideas.title: Sealed Channels
ideas.pitch: Channel messages encrypted with a key carried in the ticket, so relays and nodes passing gossip along cannot read them.
ideas.experience: You make #static as sealed. Friends join exactly as before, but the channel shows a small lock, and a gossip neighbour who happens to relay frames sees only ciphertext. When someone leaves the static, you reseal and send the new ticket to the people who stay.
ideas.audience: statics, FCs, privacy-minded players
ideas.how: Add a symmetric key to the ltroom ticket in ticket.rs and encrypt the payload inside the signed frame in proto.rs (XChaCha20-Poly1305, signature over the ciphertext). Scope::Custom topics stay random. 'Reseal' makes a new channel with a new key and sends ChannelInvite over each chosen friend link, which friends.rs already does. The plugin shows a lock in DrawList and the ticket wording changes in DrawAdd.
ideas.risks: Anyone holding the ticket still reads everything; this protects against the swarm, not against members. Removing a member is only a reseal, and old keys still read old history. A ticket format change needs a version byte and a clear message on old clients.

ideas.title: Channel Pull Timer
ideas.pitch: A countdown anyone in a channel can start, drawn on every member's screen, without touching the game's own countdown.
ideas.experience: Your raid lead types /lantern pull 10 in #static. A calm 10, 9, 8 appears on everyone's screen at the same moment, with a soft chime at zero. The game's /countdown is left alone for the party leader.
ideas.audience: statics, raid leaders, event organisers
ideas.how: Channel messages are plain text today (LanternService.SendToChannel calls RoomSend with the string). Add a small structured envelope with a reserved prefix that carries a duration, not a clock time, parsed in XivLantern.Core and tested there. Command.Parse gains 'pull <seconds> [channel]'. The plugin draws an overlay window with no inputs and a toast through the existing INotificationManager at zero. It never sends /countdown or any game command.
ideas.risks: Old clients show the envelope as a raw line, so the prefix must read sensibly as text. Relay latency makes timers drift by a few hundred milliseconds between members. People will ask for it to start the game's countdown; that is a game command and stays out.

ideas.title: Pass a Picture Along
ideas.pitch: Share a screenshot or small file with a friend or channel, peer to peer, shown as a thumbnail you choose to open.
ideas.experience: You finally clear the fight and drop the clear screenshot into #static. Everyone sees 'Alice offered clear.png, 2.1 MB'; a click fetches it straight from Alice's node and shows it in the chat pane.
ideas.audience: statics, friends, GPose photographers
ideas.how: The network half exists: lt_blob_add_file, lt_blob_offer, lt_blob_fetch and LT_EV_BLOB_OFFER/PROGRESS/DONE are in lantern.h and wrapped by LanternNode.BlobAddFile/BlobOffer/BlobFetch. The plugin needs a picker (a path field or drag from the file system), an offer line in ChatBook, fetch on click into a folder under the plugin config directory, and a thumbnail through ITextureProvider for PNG and JPEG only. For 1:1, offer over the friend link rather than a room.
ideas.risks: Decoding untrusted images in the game process is a crash and exploit surface; fetch must stay click-to-accept, capped in size, and blocked or muted peers ignored. Screenshots leak names and chat, so the offer dialog should say so. Blob storage grows on disk and needs a cleanup setting.

categories.name: Voices in the Aether
categories.tagline: Calls between friends, built so that a codec crash can never take the game down with it.

ideas.title: Ring a Friend
ideas.pitch: One-to-one voice calls: ring from the friend list, and the audio runs in a small companion process beside the game.
ideas.experience: You right-click Bob and choose Ring. His Lantern chimes with 'Alice is calling'; he answers, and you are talking, no server and no other app to open. Mute and hang up sit in the Lantern window.
ideas.audience: friends, duos, statics that do not want a separate voice app
ideas.how: Follows DESIGN.md's call plan. Signalling already exists as a spike behind the calls feature (node/calls.rs: CallRing, CallAnswer, CallHangup with an iroh://<node>/call/<id> media URL); it needs C ABI events and a MainWindow call bar. Media runs in a lantern-media sidecar using moq-native with iroh and moq-audio against PipeWire (or WASAPI on Windows), paired to the plugin's node by a one-time ticket like a friend invite and driven over a loopback friend link.
ideas.risks: None of the media path has been built; DESIGN.md lists four observable steps before anything is in the game. Shipping and starting a second executable from a Dalamud plugin is unusual and must be explicit to the player. Echo cancellation, NAT traversal for UDP media and latency are all unmeasured.

ideas.title: Voice Without the Sidecar
ideas.pitch: Try running Opus capture and playback inside lantern.dll itself, under the game's Wine, so voice needs nothing else installed.
ideas.experience: You install one plugin and nothing else. Ring a friend, and it just works, on Windows and on a Steam Deck under Proton alike.
ideas.audience: Linux and Steam Deck players, anyone who hates extra installs
ideas.how: Step 5 of DESIGN.md's call plan: build moq-audio (unsafe-libopus, cpal, sonora AEC) for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu in the same container that builds lantern.dll, repeat the WINE.md evidence method with a test prefix, and only then consider the game's prefix. Frames stay off the render thread; the plugin only sees lt_poll events for mute and level.
ideas.risks: cpal's WASAPI path under Wine goes through Wine's audio stack, whose latency and device handling vary by distro. A crash in audio code is a game crash, which is the reason the sidecar exists. It may simply not be good enough, and the honest result could be 'no'.

ideas.title: The FC Hearth
ideas.pitch: One container an FC can run on a spare box: an iroh relay, a moq relay for group calls, and an always-on node that keeps channel history.
ideas.experience: Your FC's tech person runs one command on their home server. Settings now offer 'Our relay' with its URL, the FC channel has history even when nobody else was online, and eight of you can be in a call without anyone's upload melting.
ideas.audience: FCs, communities, homelab folks
ideas.how: Relay choice already supports LT_RELAY_CUSTOM with a URL (Configuration.CustomRelayUrl, Privacy.Relay). Package iroh-relay, moq-relay and a headless lantern-cli node (the CLI already runs author mode, so a 'keeper' mode that joins listed channels and serves history snapshots fits) as one OCI image with a compose file and a README of who sees what. Group calls use the relay for fan-out per the DESIGN.md plan.
ideas.risks: Whoever runs it sees IP addresses and timing for everyone who uses it, and holds every channel's plaintext if channels are not sealed; the privacy note must name them. Home hosting means port forwarding or tunnels. Keeping three services patched is a real commitment for a volunteer.

categories.name: Letters That Find You
categories.tagline: Messages and friends that follow a person across time offline and across devices.

ideas.title: Leave It at the Post
ideas.pitch: When a friend has been offline for a while, your message also goes to their nostr inbox, so it reaches them even if you are both never online at once.
ideas.experience: You play mornings, Bob plays nights. You write 'savage lockout reset, do you want the loot?' and log off. Bob logs in at midnight and it is there, marked as arrived by post, with no second copy when your nodes do meet.
ideas.audience: friends across time zones, shift workers, returning players
ideas.how: DESIGN.md specifies it: NIP-17 kind 14 rumor, sealed and gift-wrapped to the friend's DM relays, carrying the Lantern message id so the iroh copy is dropped as a duplicate. The nostr feature already sends invites this way (nostr_send_invite, nostr_check_inbox in node/nostr.rs); extend it to texts in the outbox, then expose nostr in the C ABI, which it is not today, and add a relay list to Configuration.
ideas.risks: Relays learn who receives messages, when and how big. It needs both people to have opted into nostr keys, and the nostr secret sits unencrypted in SQLite. Relays drop old events on their own schedule, so delivery is best effort and the UI must not promise more.

ideas.title: One Friend, Every Device
ideas.pitch: A friend who plays on a PC and a Steam Deck is one entry, and messages reach whichever device they are on.
ideas.experience: Bob moves from his desk to the sofa with the Deck. His lantern stays lit under one name, and the message you sent while he was switching arrives on the Deck, not on the PC he just shut down.
ideas.audience: Steam Deck and multi-PC players
ideas.how: The core already models friends with many devices (friends and friend_devices tables) and verifies nostr device lists (nostr_publish_devices, nostr_fetch_devices, the lantern-device-claim/1 signature). What is missing is text fan-out to all devices with de-duplication by message id across them, the nostr calls in lantern-ffi and include/lantern.h, and a 'this device / add a device' page in MainWindow.DrawSettings.
ideas.risks: Delivered and read state across devices gets confusing fast (delivered to the PC, read on the Deck). Adding a device means importing the nsec on each, which moves a secret between machines. DESIGN.md lists this as the known gap because it is real work.

ideas.title: Invite by Name Card
ideas.pitch: Send a friend invite to someone's nostr npub or name@domain instead of pasting a ticket through a tell or Discord.
ideas.experience: Your friend's profile says their Lantern name is cid@example.org. You type it into Add, press Invite, and a day later they see 'Alice invited you' in their Add tab, ready to accept or ignore.
ideas.audience: players who meet outside the game, streamers with public npubs
ideas.how: nostr_send_invite and nostr_check_inbox are implemented and tested against an in-process relay (tests/nostr.rs), raising NostrInvite without redeeming anything. Add them to lantern-ffi as new LT_EV_* events, NIP-05 resolution as DESIGN.md describes, and an npub field plus pending list in MainWindow.DrawAdd. Accepting still goes through AcceptInvite, so nothing is accepted for the player.
ideas.risks: A public npub invites spam; rate limits and ignore must apply to nostr invites too. NIP-05 depends on someone's web server being up. It adds a third party (nostr relays) that the privacy note must name.

ideas.title: Lantern in Your Pocket
ideas.pitch: A small phone app that is one more of your devices, so you can see who is lit and answer a message away from the PC.
ideas.experience: You are on the bus when your phone buzzes: 'Bob: static tonight at 8?'. You answer 'yes' from the phone. At 8 you log in, and the reply is in the game window's history like any other.
ideas.audience: everyone with a phone, statics that organise during the day
ideas.how: lantern-core is plain Rust with no game dependency, and lantern-cli already runs it headless. A mobile shell (iroh runs on Android and iOS) would reuse lantern-core, pair as another device through the nostr device list (lantern-every-device), and use the nostr mailbox for wake-ups instead of a push server. Start with the CLI on a Linux phone or Termux as the proof.
ideas.risks: Mobile OSes kill background sockets, so presence and delivery need the mailbox or a push service, which reintroduces a server. App store distribution is its own project. Keys on a phone widen where the identity can be stolen from.

categories.name: The Lamplighter's Keys
categories.tagline: Identity, trust and the author channel: who you are talking to and how your keys are kept.

ideas.title: Check It Is Really Them
ideas.pitch: Four short words derived from both of your node ids that you can read to each other in game or in voice to confirm the friend is who they say.
ideas.experience: A 'Bob' redeemed your invite, but you sent it in a busy Discord. You open his entry: 'lamp moss harbour quill'. You /tell Bob in game to read his; they match, and you tick verified.
ideas.audience: anyone who shares invites in semi-public places
ideas.how: A pure function in XivLantern.Core over the two 32-byte node ids (sorted, hashed, mapped to a fixed wordlist), host-tested for symmetry. MainWindow's friend context menu shows it; a local Verified flag in Configuration adds a mark in DrawList. Display names are self-asserted (DESIGN.md), and friendship is keyed on the QUIC-authenticated NodeId, so this checks the thing that is actually authenticated.
ideas.risks: Only as good as the out-of-band check; people will tick it without comparing. A friend who reinstalls gets a new NodeId and must be verified again, which is correct but will surprise them.

ideas.title: Lock the Lantern
ideas.pitch: Optionally protect the device key (and nostr key) in the node's database with a passphrase, entered when you turn Lantern on.
ideas.experience: You share a PC with a flatmate. With a passphrase set, /lantern on asks for it once per session; the SQLite file on its own is useless to anyone who copies it.
ideas.audience: shared PCs, privacy-minded players
ideas.how: DESIGN.md's threat model says the key sits unencrypted like an SSH key with no passphrase. Wrap the identity row and the nostr_secret profile row with a key derived by Argon2id, add an unlock parameter to lt_config (an lt_node_open error code for 'locked'), and a passphrase prompt in MainWindow.DrawWelcome before LanternService.Start. Existing databases migrate on first set.
ideas.risks: A forgotten passphrase loses the identity for good; there is deliberately no recovery. Auto-start at plugin load (config.Enabled) can no longer be silent. The ABI version must bump.

ideas.title: Moving House
ideas.pitch: Export your identity and friend list to one encrypted file and import it on a new PC, so friends do not have to re-add you.
ideas.experience: New PC day. You export from the old one, copy the file on a USB stick, import on the new one, and your lantern lights for the same friends under the same node id, as if nothing changed.
ideas.audience: anyone who reinstalls or upgrades
ideas.how: The store already holds everything: identity, profile, friends, friend_devices, blocked. Add export and import to lantern-core (a passphrase-encrypted SQLite backup plus a schema version check), expose them in lantern-ffi, and put two buttons in MainWindow.DrawSettings. Saved channel tickets live in the Dalamud Configuration and would be included from the C# side.
ideas.risks: Running two copies of the same NodeId at once confuses friends' links and presence; import should refuse while another node with that id is online, which is hard to know. The export file is a full identity and must be treated like a private key.

ideas.title: News From the Lamplighter
ideas.pitch: Each release posts its changelog entry to the author channel as a signed announcement, so players who opted in hear about fixes in game.
ideas.experience: You log in and the Announcements pane has a new verified line: 'Test build 0.2: channel invites fixed; please run /lantern selftest and send what it prints.' A button beside it opens Write to the author.
ideas.audience: players in the author channel, testers
ideas.how: tools/release.sh and tools/changelog.py already produce the player-facing entry from changelog.json. Add a step that signs it offline with the lantern CLI's author sign command (crates/lantern-cli/src/author.rs, which prints an ltannounce line with a growing --seq) and hands that line to the author node's /announce, per docs/AUTHOR.md. The plugin already verifies and shows announcements (LT_EV_ANNOUNCEMENT, AuthorChat).
ideas.risks: AuthorIdentity.cs is still empty, so nothing can be verified until the author does the AUTHOR.md setup. Signing must stay on the author's machine and never move into CI. Too many announcements will get the channel muted.
